sections.html:
Curry County's seat is Clovis, a Llano Estacado town near the Texas line that counted 38,567 people in 2020. US 60, US 70 and US 84 pass through town. Cannon Air Force Base sits roughly 7 to 8 miles west of the center. Railroad roots go back to 1906, and BNSF still operates a division point and big freight yard here.

Most local paychecks trace back to Cannon, the rail yard, farming and dairy processing, or a handful of manufacturers. When one of those shifts, house sales feel it.

sections.h2: Cannon Air Force Base and military sellers
sections.html:
Cannon is the largest single factor. The 27th Special Operations Wing fact sheet puts the workforce at about 6,500 military and civilian personnel at Cannon and the nearby Melrose Air Force Range. It also counts more than 7,800 military personnel, civilian employees and family members on the base population side, plus about 4,000 retirees.

Orders set the pace for service families, so a sale linked to a permanent change of station has a hard end date. VA-financed buyers go through an appraisal and condition review, which gets difficult when the roof is failing or the foundation has moved. Cash buyers skip that review.

sections.h2: Wind, hail, snow and tornado exposure
sections.html:
Wind never really stops in Clovis, a dry plains town on the southern edge of Tornado Alley. Gusts often pass 30 miles per hour and the average speed is about 12 across open, flat ground. Severe thunderstorms arrive in spring, heavy rain shows up on summer evenings, and snow lingers for several weeks in January and February.

The town has almost no storm runoff system, so snowmelt and heavy rain can cause minor street flooding. A low lot or a garage floor level with the street will draw questions.

  • Roofs face wind and storm exposure all year. Lenders may want lifted flashing, missing shingles or old patches repaired.
  • Heating and cooling both get a workout, with a January daily low near 22 degrees and a July daily high near 91.
  • Wind can take out fences, sheds and carports, so list any repairs you made.

With a cash buyer, the cost of these problems is built into the offer and nobody argues about repairs. A listing rarely avoids that argument.

Two payments make up the yearly Curry County bill: November 10 and April 10. Mailing happens by November 1, and paying at least half by December 10 avoids interest and penalty.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for the tax year
April 10Second half due
May 10Final day for the second half, no charges

December 10Final day for the first half or the full bill

Roughly 27,000 real property parcels sit on the Assessor's rolls, each taxed on 33.33 percent of appraised value after exemptions. Four school and tax districts divide the county (Clovis, Texico, Melrose and Grady), and the one covering your address shapes your rate.

Leave taxes unpaid past three years and the property can go to the State of New Mexico and then to public auction. If back taxes are hanging over a house you want to sell, tell your title company right away, because the lien must clear at closing. The Curry County Treasurer, 417 Gidding Street, Suite 150, can show you what is still open.

sections.h2: How a sale changes the tax value
sections.html:
A sale gives the county a chance to reassess a Clovis house at market value, so the next owner's bill often climbs. Statute 7-36-21.2 limits annual residential increases to 3 percent over the prior year, or 6.1 percent over two years if that is higher, but the limit falls away in the year after ownership changes.

Some transfers do not count as a change of ownership: certain ones between spouses, to a child living in the home, or into a revocable trust. An ordinary sale is not among them. Smart buyers ask how long the seller has owned, since a long-held house can carry a valuation well under its sale price.

Timing matters for you. Each tax year is valued as of January 1, and title companies usually split the year's tax between the two sides at closing, so get that split in writing. After the deed records, the Assessor's Deeds Specialist can explain what the Real Property Transfer Declaration Affidavit needs.

sections.h2: City rules, nuisance reports and permits
sections.html:
Non-emergency complaints in Clovis go through a 311 portal, Clovis NM Works, where neighbors can report alley debris or overgrown lots with a photo and without giving a name. Before listing an inherited or vacant house, look for open complaints tied to the address.

Building Safety and Code Compliance share a city department, and permit applications go through its online portal. Unpermitted deck, roof or electrical work can stall a conventional sale because lenders and inspectors may ask for records. Water issues go to Epcor Water and outages to Xcel Energy, so take final meter readings on closing day.

  • Check the city code on Municode for yard, junk vehicle and structure rules.
  • Gather permit records for any work after you bought.
  • Ask your title company about unpaid tax or utility balances.

A few items save headaches once you have an accepted offer. Order your payoff statement if there is a mortgage. Gather the deed, the latest Curry County bill and receipts for both halves. Bring permit records for any roof, deck or electrical work. Ask the title company whether unpaid tax or utility balances show up on its search.

On the day itself, expect to sign a deed and a settlement statement, hand over keys and any garage openers, and take final meter readings. The proceeds are what remains after the mortgage, liens and prorated tax are paid.

sections.h2: Who buys in Clovis and which sale route fits
sections.html:
Three buyer groups dominate: military households, local families, and investors who rent to both. Local families usually need a bank loan and a standard inspection. Investors paying cash close sooner and take the house as it is.

The open market can fetch the top price for a clean, updated house, though showings, inspection requests, appraisal risk and commission come with it. Selling for cash trades some price for speed and certainty, and fits probate, orders to move, tax debt, a tenant who will not leave, or repairs the family cannot fund.

Wherever you land, get the offer in writing, pin down who pays each closing cost, and use a New Mexico title company for closing. We make no promise on price, because it depends on the house, its location and the work needed.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in Clovis?
faqs.a: Title work sets the pace, not a lender. Clean title can close within weeks, and liens, probate or missing signatures stretch that out.

faqs.q: Do I owe Curry County property tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, for any year you owned it on January 1, plus any balance still open. The title company normally collects what is unpaid at closing.

faqs.q: Does a Clovis sale raise the property tax for the buyer?
faqs.a: Often. The 3 percent yearly cap on residential increases falls away the year after ownership changes, so the county can reassess at market value.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clovis house that needs a new roof?
faqs.a: Yes. Storm and wind damage are routine on the plains, and cash buyers typically accept the roof as it is and adjust their offer.

faqs.q: What if the house is inherited and still in a parent's name?
faqs.a: Someone must have legal authority to sell, typically through probate or a court-approved personal representative. See a New Mexico attorney first, then ask the title company which documents it wants.
